**Verdict: REVISE.** This applies to digest f8584a958eddaf8f1811a2a01c4b72a02e12f9e6456bb01d32e15a0656bd42f9 at commit 1f12c58a6. One item blocks; the rest are optional. A later PASS would cover running the pilot only, not production adoption or any performance claim.

**What I could and couldn't read:**
- Reading `~/.codex/skills/experiment-preflight/SKILL.md` and `~/agent-config` was permission-denied. I built the checklist from the global AGENTS.md experiment rules plus `docs/agent/ara-evidence-policy.md:132-159`. The numbering is mine and may not match the skill's 26 items.
- I have no shell, so I accepted the bindings on the strength of your rerun and did not verify them myself.

## Alignment with Q1 ("Dann bitte nyström Nutzung untersuchen und verbessern")
The pilot is aligned with the question.
- **"Untersuchen" (investigate):** the traces separate the first rejection, the cost stop, numerical invalidity and cached suppression. They are produced whatever the verdict, so no gate blocks this part of the answer.
- **"Verbessern" (improve):** tested with one minimal candidate (drop the σ² memory) under an equivalence screen and a time screen. This is the smallest slice: a one-line change on the existing runner and fixture.
- **Reading of "improve":** "same endpoint, less total work" is the packet's interpretation, but it is stated (`layer-b.md:9`).
- **Scope consequence:** "less work" is judged only against the suppressing baseline over 20 iterations. Even a FOLLOW-UP verdict says nothing about Nyström versus Auto.

## Reconstruction compared with the packet's intent
The cells, commands, units, gates, controls, stop rules and report all match. Two code facts strengthen the packet:
- A rejected attempt calls `Resize`, which zeroes every output and per-row buffer (`EStep.cpp:1205-1213, 1674`). Candidate and baseline therefore stay bitwise identical until the first accepted retry on a draw the baseline suppressed. So an increase in accepted count implies H1, and floor parity carries over to the candidate's fallback iterations.
- Parameter validation accepts both control configurations (`CoherentPointDrift.cpp:648-653`).

The test logs confirm `layer-b.md:54-57`: baseline passes 8/8, the counterexample fails on baseline (policy 1 instead of 5), and the candidate passes 29/29.

Mismatches:
- **M1:** `layer-b.md:34-35` promises counts by rejection class. `report()` only gives total attempts, suppressed draws, cost stops and raw log lines (`diagnose.py:140-145`). Numerical versus sampled-error rejections are left to manual reading. A NaN error without an `invalid_*` line (eigen failure or top ≤ 0) has no named class.
- **M2:** "Auto has zero Nyström iterations" (`:43`) cannot fail, because Auto never selects Nyström (`EStep.cpp:1688-1714`). It is a wiring check, not a positive control.
- **M3:** The INVALID strings don't name the failing cell (`diagnose.py:84-89`).
- **M4:** The technical validity check (`:62-65`) covers 5 of the 7 native configurations.

## Blocking
**B1 — the technical test does not cover the final configuration.** The floor control (4096 landmarks) and the negative control (2 landmarks, error limit 1e+300) were never executed (`driver-selftest.txt:3`).
- **Floor:** almost trivial. It hits the cost stop and runs the ordinary fallback.
- **Negative:** runs a path nobody has exercised. Accepted 2-landmark E-steps feed the Bayesian M-step. A NumericalFailure there exits with code 3 (`runner:210-214`), which stops the whole plan at cell 3 (`diagnose.py:257`).
- **Rule:** the global rules require the real path with the final configuration before any run. Skipping it is a weaker exception that only the user can grant.
- **Fix:** run both control cells technical-only against a technical Auto reference. Assert exit 0, success, complete positions and finite traces, without inspecting values.
- **Optional extra assertion:** pass/fail on the control's precondition "≥1 accepted Nyström iteration". In the baseline binary, a negative rejected at draw 0 is suppressed for the rest of the run, which makes the whole pilot INVALID.

## Clarifications that need a packet revision (I am not treating them as permission)
- **c11 ("INVALID on accuracy failure is a negative candidate outcome").** This is not in the frozen packet. It is also wrong when the failing cell is a baseline arm: then the production Nyström path itself fails the screen and the comparison can't be interpreted. It is equally wrong when the failing cell is the floor, since that is an instrument failure. Either freeze a per-cell interpretation or withdraw the clarification. The frozen "retain the negative finding" (`:50`) already rules out discarding data or rerunning.
- **"If the negative fails execution, the plan stops technically."** Accepting this is the B1 waiver, so it needs the user's explicit decision.
- **Already frozen, no revision needed:**
  - scope and truth score: `:10, :26-28`
  - negative control invalidates the comparison: `:44-45`
  - sampled oracle unchanged: `:46-48`
  - floor parity: `:43-44`
  - repeats are a screen only: `:37-40`
  - timeout and failure override: `layer-a.md:38-42`, `diagnose.py:70, 260-263`
  - outputs retained: `:71`
  - follow-up only: `:49-51`
  - The 1800 s acknowledgement needs no revision unless you change the budget.
  - I withdraw my Layer A Q7.

## Optional (worth folding in, since the digest changes anyway)
- **O1:** Add self-test assertions for the parity/sensitivity line (`diagnose.py:82`, which "never silently pass" rests on), the determinism gate and the count gate. They are correct by inspection but not asserted.
- **O2:** Tabulate rejection classes per draw (fixes M1).
- **O3:** Check the technical batch's total time against 1800 s, without looking at per-arm times, or raise the cap. The alarm also covers 11 manifest hashings and repeated re-rendering of the report: the figures for every completed cell are re-rendered after each cell, 66 cell renders in total.
- **O4:** Consider running the negative control in the candidate binary. That gives it up to 20 chances to be accepted instead of one.
- **O5:** State that Auto's single cold-start time is not a comparator.
- **O6:** Have the report say "mechanism not exercised" when a baseline variant has no suppressed draw, instead of only DO NOT ADOPT.

## Checklist
1. Verbatim question, goal and shortest path: ✓ (`:3-10`)
2. Every cell maps to Q1: ✓
3. H1–H3 with predictions: ✓ (`:12-18`)
4. Signature of an ineffective method: ✓ (`:19-20`)
5. Kill condition: ✓ (`:49-51`)
6. Positive controls: partial. Floor parity is real; M2 is not a control.
7. Negative control: ✓ in logic (a negative that fell back is identical to the floor, ≤ 2e-4, so INVALID). Sensitivity is tested only at gross scale; prospective.
8. Null arm: ✓ (baseline with identical diagnostics, hashes reported)
9. Collapse and degenerate outcomes: ✓ (no claim of successful registration)
10. Repetitions: ✓ (two passes in reverse order, bitwise repeat gate)
11. Detection limit: ✓ for timing (10%, stated relatively). The endpoint screen is not calibrated below gross error.
12. Skipped controls justified: ✓ (`:23-31`)
13. Cheap null probes: ✓ (synthetic self-test). Real timing noise comes from the pilot itself, which is allowed.
14. Technical test with the final configuration: ✗ (B1)
15. Metrics with units: ✓
16. Frozen gates: ✓ (self-test coverage is partial, see O1)
17. Command, resolved config and data: ✓
18. Bounded plan: ✓ (11 cells, seed 1)
19. Frozen after the last commit: ✓
20. Start check against the frozen plan: ✓ (`diagnose.py:232-248`)
21. Timeouts in code: ✓ (`test-timeout.py` tests the SIGALRM path)
22. Budget: specified, but not shown to be sufficient (O3)
23. Two fresh full reviews on the same digest: in progress
24. Report contents: ✓ except M1
25. Surprises: ✓ the frozen cells continue (`:71`). The repository's "surprise voids the plan" rule (`ara-evidence-policy.md:186-189`) applies to the next plan, not this one.
26. Post-run: raw outputs and negative results retained, no adaptive rerun: ✓ (`:49-51, :75`)
